source: Official Form 204, “List of Creditors Who Have the 30 Largest Unsecured Claims and Are Not Insiders,” filed as part of Docket #1 (Voluntary Petition, pages 28-29) on 08/30/2026, signed by Robert Albergotti, CTO.
note: The form itself only labels each claim's 'nature' as printed (mostly “Trade Vendor”, one “Debt”). The 'likely_type' field is our own inference from the company name, industry, and cross-reference against other filings in this case — not a classification the filing itself makes — so treat it as a reasonable guess, not a confirmed fact.

creditors.name: Robert H McWilliams
creditors.notes: By far the largest unsecured claim in the case and the only individual on the list. Identified from Noble's own press archive: McWilliams was CEO of Federal Resources Supply Company (grew it from $80M to $350M+ revenue, 2012-2017), then became its President and Chairman in 2018 (Noble.com press release, 6/25/2018). Noble acquired Federal Resources in October 2021. The First Day Declaration (Docket #15) discloses a $36M unsecured 'Seller Note' issued to 'former stakeholders of Federal Resources Supply Company' as acquisition consideration — this $32M claim, classified as 'Debt' rather than 'Trade Vendor,' is almost certainly McWilliams' share of that Seller Note (or closely related deferred consideration), not a trade/vendor obligation. Not stated explicitly as such in any filing we've read — inferred from the press release plus the Seller Note disclosure, not confirmed by a document that names him as the noteholder. His current email domain (wrighttoolcompany.com) suggests he has since moved on to Wright Tool Company, an industrial tool maker unrelated to Noble.
